hypothesis: In a broad species-level census of gametic (haploid, n) chromosome numbers, most species have n between 6 and 16, with fewer species below 6 and still fewer above 16.
pass_criterion: Using one value of n per species (the median of its recorded gametic counts), at least 70% of species have 6 <= n <= 16. The fraction with n < 6 is under 15%. The fraction with n > 16 is smaller than the fraction with n < 6. All three conditions must hold.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 50% of species have 6 <= n <= 16, or the fraction with n > 16 is equal to or larger than the fraction with n < 6. Either result refutes the claim. Results between these thresholds (50-70% in range, with the ordering holding) are reported as inconclusive and the claim is not counted as confirmed.
interpretation: Thompson's 'germ-nuclei' are the reduced (gametic, haploid) nuclei, so the quantity tested is n, not the somatic 2n. 'Few' and 'fewer still' are read as minority fractions, with the below-six tail larger than the above-sixteen tail. 'Most' is read as at least 70% for a pass. The unit is the species, to avoid weighting by how often a species has been counted. The 1917 view is that the range is narrow; modern polyploidy and genome-size work (many plant species with n > 16) may contradict it. The scope is 'plants and animals'. CCDB covers mainly plants (angiosperms, gymnosperms, ferns, bryophytes), so this test covers only the plant half of the claim. A refutation in plants refutes the generalization as stated, but a pass would not establish the animal half. 2n values in the database must be halved, or excluded if only 2n is given and ploidy is ambiguous.

dataset.name: Chromosome Counts Database (CCDB)
dataset.publisher: Tel Aviv University (Rice et al. 2015, New Phytologist)
dataset.why_it_fits: CCDB is a curated public compilation of published chromosome counts, with a searchable and downloadable interface. Fields used: species name (genus and species), gametophytic count n, sporophytic count 2n, and the source reference. Deriving a per-species median n gives the distribution needed to compute the fractions below 6, from 6 to 16, and above 16. It tests the claim for plants only. No DOI is given because none is known.
